project.title: Mass spectrometry of PtGtsf1 interacted proteins in Paramecium tetraurelia
project.projectDescription: PtGtsf1 was fused with FlagHA and induced to express in Paramecium tetraurelia. The interacted proteins of PtGtsf1 was obtained by immunoprecipitation with anti-HA antibody, followed with mass spectrometry to identify the proteins. Meanwhile, FlagHA without PtGtsf1 was expressed in Paramecium tetraurelia as control and was performed with same procedures as PtGtsf1-FlagHA. By comparing the enrichment of proteins in PtGtsf1-FlagHA and control, the interacted proteins of PtGtsf1 in Paramecium tetraurelia were identified.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: 1.In gel digsestion  Bands of interest were cut off and washed with ddH2O2 for 10 minutes. The gel pieces were destained by in-gel digestion and decolorization buffer(50% acetonitrile containing 25mM NH4HCO3) for 20 minutes. Then the acetonitrile were added for dehydrating and removed by vacuuming when the gel pieces were completely white.10 mM dithiothreitol were added and and the gel were incubated at 56℃ for 1 hour. Then the excess dithiothreitol were removed and the gel were incubated in 55mM iodoacetamide at room temperature in a dark room for 45 min. Next the excess IAM were removed and the gel were washed by 25mM NH4HCO3 for 10 min. Then the gel were washed by in-gel digestion and decolorization buffer for 10 min. The acetonitrile were added for dehydrating and removed by vacuuming when the gel was completely white. The 1μg/μL trypsin solution was diluted 15 times with 25 mM NH4HCO3 and added to the dehydrated gel pieces for digesting at 37℃ overnight. Next day 0.1% formic acid were used to stop the digestion. 10ul solution containg peptides were used for mass spectrometer detecting. 2. LC-MS Analysis The peptides were are separated by the UltiMate3000 RSLCnano ultra-high performance liquid system. Mobile phase A is an aqueous solution containing 0.1% formic acid, mobile phase B is an aqueous solution containing 0.1% formic acid and 98% acetonitrile. Liquid phase gradient setting were: 0~6 mins -- 5%~8% phase B; 7~40 mins -- 8%~30% phase B; 41~45 mins -- 30%~60% phase B; 46~48 mins -- 60%~80% phase B; 49~56 mins -- 80% phase B; 56~58 mins -- 80%-5% phase B; 58~65 mins -- 5% phase B; The flow rate is maintained at 400 nL/min. The peptides were then analyzed by the Thermo ScientificTM Q ExactiveTM mass spectrometer. The ion source voltage was 1.8 kV, and the peptide precursors and the fragments were detected and analyzed using high-resolution Orbitrap. The scanning range of MS was set to 350-2000 for full scan, and the scanning resolution was set to 70,000. Data Dependent Acquisition (DDA) procedure were used for data acquisition. The top 20 peptides with the highest signal intensity were then selected for MS/MS using NCE setting as 28 and the fragments were detected by Heated capillary disssociation(HCD) at a resolution of 17,500.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: The resulting MS/MS data were processed using MASCOT2.3.0. Tandem mass spectra were searched against uniprot20160315. Trypsin was specified as cleavage enzyme allowing up to 2 missing cleavages. Mass error was set to 15 ppm for precursor ions and 20 mmu for fragment ions. Carbamidomethyl on Cys were specified as fixed modification, Gln->pyro-Glu (N-term Q) and oxidation on Met was specified as variable modification. Peptide ion score was set > 20.
